deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as reconstructed from this page and the neighbouring ones. Grothendieck has an arrangement Σ of n pseudo-lines D_1,…,D_n in the (real) projective plane. He considers a cellular space 𝒳 whose points are 'positions' of an extra pseudo-line D relative to Σ. This is close to what is now called the extension space of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Σ, i.e. its single-element extensions by a pseudo-line. Inside it there is a wall/discriminant locus K, some of whose components are 'exceptional', one for each D_i ∈ Σ (the place where D coincides with D_i). Over 𝒳 there is a local system with fibre F_D attached to the polygon Pol(D) (= Pℓ(D)). Pol(D) is the cyclic polygon cut out on D by its n intersection points with Σ. This gives a monodromy representation u: π1(𝒳, F_D) → Aut(Pol(D)). Several sign characters of π1 are in play: χ_X, χ_s, χ_o, the orientation character χ_𝒳 of the cell complex 𝒳, and a 'combinatorial' parity character χ_c. On the previous page he established χ_X χ_s χ_o = 1 and χ_𝒳 = χ_o χ_c, and chose χ_X, χ_s, χ_c as the fundamental ones.

This page computes these invariants on generators of π1. There are two kinds of fundamental loops.
(a) The loop ℓ_{D_i} crossing once the exceptional component of K attached to D_i ∈ Σ, i.e. D sweeps over D_i. Its monodromy u(ℓ_{D_i}) is the cyclic translation by n−1 of the n-gon Pol(D), oriented by the relative position of D near D_i. On it χ_X = +1 and χ_s = (−1)^{n−1}. The value (−1)^{n−1} is the sign of an n-cycle. An earlier, crossed-out entry χ_c(ℓ_{D_i}) = 1 is struck.
(b) A half-loop around a point of X, which may lie in a face, on an edge, or at a vertex. Its monodromy is the reflection of Pol(D) fixing the corresponding point, of sign −1. Rotations together with all reflections generate the full dihedral symmetry group. Hence u_D: π1(𝒳, F_D) → Aut(F_D) is surjective ('ouf !').

Second paragraph (*): χ_c is trivial. Let sing_D be the number of vertices of Σ (crossing points of the arrangement) lying on D. For any path c from D to D′ he claims poids(c) ≡ sing_{D′} − sing_D (mod 2). The proof is by reduction to paths of length 1, where it is immediate; a 'sweep' (balayage) across a line D_i ∈ Σ has weight 2. So closed loops have even weight and χ_c = 1. Consequently χ_𝒳 = χ_X: the orientation character of 𝒳 equals χ_X, and up to the relations only χ_X and χ_s remain as independent characters. He ends by proposing to look at a concrete case ('… de P₂ / D₂').

Purpose: understand the topology (fundamental group, orientability, monodromy) of the space of pseudo-lines that can be added to a given arrangement. This is in service of a combinatorial-topological classification of pseudo-line systems.
errors: The parity formula poids(c) ≡ sing_{D'} − sing_D is only sketched ('triviale' for length-1 paths); the notion of 'poids' is defined on earlier pages, so it cannot be fully verified here, but the conclusion χ_c = 1 is consistent with the remark already added at the end of the previous page.

Surjectivity of u_D is asserted from rotations by n−1 plus reflections at faces, edges and vertices. This is correct for the dihedral group of an n-gon, since n−1 is coprime to n. It tacitly assumes Aut(F_D) is exactly the dihedral group of Pol(D).

ideas.what: Space of positions of an extra pseudo-line relative to an arrangement Σ, with a monodromy action of its π1 on the polygon cut out on the new line
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (single-element extensions by a pseudo-line) and its monodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (extensions of oriented matroids, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler (extension spaces, 1993); Goodman–Pollack (pseudo-line arrangements)

ideas.what: Computation of the monodromy generators: crossing an exceptional wall gives rotation by n−1, half-loops give reflections, so the monodromy group is the full dihedral group
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of a polygon bundle over the extension space; surjectivity onto Aut(n-gon)

ideas.what: Orientation character of the cell complex 𝒳 expressed via the sign characters (χ_𝒳 = χ_X after showing the parity character χ_c is trivial, using a parity count of arrangement vertices on D)
ideas.modern_name: Orientation character / orientability of a cellular moduli space; parity invariant via number of vertices on a pseudo-line

missed.claim: Grothendieck, in 1983–84, treats the space of single-pseudo-line extensions of an arrangement as a topological object (cell complex / 'stack' 𝒳). He computes its fundamental group action, its orientation character, and the monodromy on the polygon of the added line. This predates the oriented-matroid literature on the topology of extension spaces (Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993; the Extension Space Conjecture), and the monodromy/orientation viewpoint is not standard there.
missed.quote: u_D : π1(𝒳, F_D) → Aut(F_D) est surjectif ouf ! … il n'y a pas d'autre caractère !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a monodromy-theoretic, local-system point of view on extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, a topic where the topology (e.g. connectivity, homotopy type) is still delicate. It is of historical interest as an independent and early approach.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations themselves are elementary. The interest lies in Grothendieck independently studying the topology and monodromy of pseudo-line extension spaces in 1983–84, a viewpoint absent from his published work and only partly echoed in later oriented-matroid literature.
transcription_corrections: 'χ_×' should almost certainly be read 'χ_X' (in a) and in the final boxed formula, so the box reads χ_𝒳 = χ_X.
'correspondant à : 6 produits D_i ∈ Σ' likely reads 'correspondant à la ps.-droite D_i ∈ Σ' (abbreviation for pseudo-droite).
'pour une pr. D donnée' likely 'pour une ps.-droite D donnée'.
'Le point fixé de ce point dans Pol(D) ont signe par u(ℓ)' is better read as: the symmetry of Pol(D) fixing that point is given by u(ℓ), of sign −1.
'(dans le sens de l'orientation de la position rel.' probably 'position relative de D voisine de D_i'.
In the crossed-out part of (a), 'valeurs des caractères fondamentaux' — 'caractères' is struck through and rewritten above, not a separate word.
Final line probably 'regardons ce que ça donne pour une ps.-droite de P₂ / pour 𝔻₂'; it is uncertain.
